# PLAN — iteration 3
## Current state assessment
Iteration 2 is the verified best at 4 LUTs and 5 FFs, with WNS 0.731 ns and WHS 0.176 ns; both timing slacks are nonnegative. Since the incumbent is timing-feasible, iteration 3 must strictly reduce routed LUT use to improve the `minimize_luts` objective. Iteration 1 tied at 6 LUTs, so repeating its logic is not useful.

## Hypothesis
A 3-bit maximal-length LFSR timer with a terminal-state hold may use fewer LUTs than the incumbent’s binary increment and saturation logic while preserving the 8-cycle debounce interval.

## Instruction for generator
Keep the module interface and `// @latency 0` annotation, and replace the binary `count` increment/saturation pattern with a 3-bit LFSR sequence: load a seed when `noisy != candidate`, advance through six states on subsequent stable cycles, then hold the terminal state. Update `clean_reg` from the stable input only on the edge after the terminal state is reached, preserving the existing synchronous active-high reset and candidate tracking behavior. Ensure the change restarts the interval on every sampled input transition and check the 7-cycle and 8-cycle boundary cases; promote only if all fixed verification gates pass and routed LUT use is strictly below 4.
